summary: Independently verified the HRMS Payslip Module 6-digit authorization layer end-to-end. Backend: authored /app/backend/tests/test_payslip_auth_layer.py (13 tests, all pass in ~2m12s) covering (1) fresh-admin BEFORE verification all 6 admin payslip endpoints return 403 {error:'payslip_auth_required'} with NO monetary/salary fields in the body — GET /payslips/templates|/assignments|/generated?month=2026-07|/adjustments/summary?month=2026-07 and POST /payslips/calculate|/payslips/generate; (2) verify semantics: wrong 6-digit code -> 401 with generic 'Invalid authorization code. Please try again.' (no closeness/timing hint), 4-digit code -> 400 length error, correct '082026' -> 200 and every admin payslip endpoint then returns 200 for that session; (3) session scope: a fresh login yields a new session_id whose /payslip-security/status shows verified=false and payslip endpoints 403 again; (4) brute force: 4 wrong codes return 401, 5th returns 429 lock message, /status shows failed_attempts=5 + locked_until, correct code while locked still returns 429; after clearing payslip_auth_attempts via mongo, a correct code returns 200 and resets failed_attempts to 0; (5) employee (madhan.s) unaffected — /payslips/my returns 200, all admin payslip endpoints return 403, /payslip-security/status|settings return 403, and knowing the code via /payslip-security/verify grants NOTHING (403); (6) no plaintext leakage — code '082026' never appears in /payslip-security/status or /settings responses, only auth_code_hash+auth_code_salt live in payslip_security_settings (no unexpected keys), and db.payslip_security_audit records action=payslip_auth_verified|payslip_auth_failed|payslip_auth_lockout each with user_id+user_name+timestamp and NO code. Also grep-verified 082026 is absent from /var/log/supervisor/backend*.log and /app/frontend/src/. Regression: /app/backend/tests/test_rbac_isolation.py + test_rbac_body_leaks.py 62/62 pass unchanged. Frontend UI (admin on /payslips): modal (data-testid='payslip-auth-modal') renders, input (data-testid='payslip-auth-code-input') is autofocused, type=password (masked), maxLength=6, digits-only enforced (typed 'abc12x3' -> value '123'); no salary text visible behind modal; wrong code triggers backend 401; correct '082026' unlocks and the Payslips page body then contains 'Payslip'; navigating /dashboard -> /payslips does NOT re-prompt; Settings shows the 'Payslip Security' tab (data-testid='tab-payslip-security'/'payslip-security-tab') with a Regenerate button, no '082026' anywhere, and no 'view/show/reveal current code' affordance; logout + fresh admin login re-shows the modal. Final mongo state left clean: payslip_security_settings version=1, last_regenerated_at=null, payslip_auth_attempts collection emptied. STRICT PROHIBITION observed — POST /api/payslip-security/regenerate was never called.

integration_issues.flow: Payslip auth wrong-code error toast timing
integration_issues.issue: Playwright observation: after Enter with a wrong code the backend responded 401 in <1s but data-testid='payslip-auth-error' was not attached within the 2s post-Enter wait in the test script. Manually re-testing the same flow with an extra 2s wait shows the error banner does render. This is a race with React state batching, not a functional bug — no fix required.

critical_code_review_comments: payslip_security.py returns 400 for length errors with detail 'Enter a valid 6-digit authorization code.' — matches the ask. Consider also asserting request Content-Type application/json to avoid form-encoded probes bypassing Pydantic-less body parsing (currently `payload: dict = Body(...)` accepts empty body only via 422 — verified).

payslip_auth_guard.py exempts ^/api/payslip-security/ and ^/api/payslips/my$ correctly; PDF endpoints like /api/payslips/{id}/pdf sit under the protected regex — verified 403 before verify. Employees have role='employee' JWT claim so guard short-circuits — verified from /payslips/my 200.
server.py continues to be 19.7k lines; unrelated to this ticket but worth splitting.

Regeneration commit-after-send + version bump + delete_many on payslip_auth_sessions is a clean, race-safe design. `send_hrms_email(..., force=True)` returning falsy correctly aborts the rotation, so a mail failure can never lock the admin out (design verified statically; the live endpoint was NOT invoked per user directive).

It has autouse-module fixtures that wipe payslip_auth_attempts before and after the run so it is idempotent and won't lock the admin out.
